THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.775/2014 dated 14.10.2016, the insurance company has preferred this appeal.
2. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident.

It is the case of the claimants that on 12.04.2014 at about 4.30 a.m. the deceased was travelling as a coolie, as a loader in goods vehicle and the said vehicle was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, the said vehicle dashed to bridge wall on the road side and the deceased was injured and shifted NC: 2023:KHC:38825 to hospital where he succumbed to the injuries.
According to the claimant, the deceased was working as coolie/mason and earning an amount of Rs.12,000/- per month.
It is the case of the insurance company that he was a gratuitous passenger in a goods vehicle, as such the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
As per the policy, only the driver and another person was covered and as such the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

The court below has observed that though it is the case of the insurance company that the deceased was a gratuitous passenger, they have not adduced any document in support of their case, that he was not a loader in the said vehicle.
The court below has also observed that the policy is a comprehensive policy and risk are covered.

Considering the fact that the deceased was travelling in the said vehicle as loader and unloader and as there is policy which covers another person apart from driver of the vehicle, the Tribunal had held that the insurance company and owner of the vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
When it comes to the compensation, as per the Post- Mortem report, the claimant was aged between 60-70 years.

The court below considering the income at an amount of Rs.7,500/- and age at 50 years by applying the multiplier 13 had granted an amount of Rs.7,80,000/-, under the head of loss of dependency and towards love and affection an amount of Rs.20,000/- was granted.
Towards Funeral expenses an amount of Rs.20,000/- was granted and an amount of Rs.10,000/- was granted towards transportation.
Altogether compensation of an amount of Rs.8,70,000/- was granted.
3. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that as per the Post-Mortem Report, he is aged between 60-70 years.
In that case, the court below went wrong in considering the age at 50 years and applying the multiplier 13.
It is further submitted that he was a gratuitous passenger and the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.

This aspect was also not NC:
2023:KHC:38825 considered by the Tribunal.
It is submitted that the court below without any basis had taken the income at an amount of Rs.7,500/- which is on the higher side.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the date of birth of the deceased is 1st October 1955.
It is submitted that the deceased is not a gratuitous passenger and basing on the evidence available, the court below had rightly considered the same and granted the compensation.
He further submits that no grounds are made out for interference of the award passed by the MACT.
5. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
According to the claimants, the deceased was working as loader and unloader and after unloading the goods and while coming back, accident had taken place.
According to the insurance company, he was a gratuitous passenger.

In that case, it is for the insurance company to adduce the NC:
2023:KHC:38825 evidence and no such evidence is adduced by the insurance company.

Hence,
basing on the evidence on record, the Tribunal had rightly held that he is not a gratuitous passenger.
Secondly along with the driver another person is also covered under the policy.
In that matter, the court below had rightly fixed the liability both on the owner of vehicle as well as the insurance company and this court finds no reasons to interfere with the same.
6. Coming to the compensation, when the age of the deceased as per the Post-Mortem report is between 60-70 years, the court below without any basis had taken the age at 50 years.
Hence, this court is inclined to consider the age of the deceased as per his date of birth i.e., 01.10.1955, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged 58 years old.
Then coming to the income, the accident had taken place in the year 2014, considering the minimum wages, this court is inclined to take an amount of Rs.8,500/- as income.
As his age is 58 years, he is entitled for 10% future prospects, it comes to NC: 2023:KHC:38825 an amount of Rs.850/-., i.e., Rs.8,500 + Rs.850/- = Rs.9,350/-.
Though it is stated that there are three claimants generally 1/3rd has to be deducted.
In this case except the wife, other two persons are major children who are aged about 30 years and 28 years respectively.
The major children cannot be considered as dependents on the deceased.
Hence, this court is inclined to deduct 50% towards personal expenses.
Then his contribution to the family is calculated as Rs.4,675/- x 12 x 9 which comes to Rs.5,04,900/-.
Towards loss of dependency this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.5,04,900/-.
Towards consortium for the two children and the wife, Rs.44,000/- x 3 an amount of Rs.1,32,000/- is granted.
Towards funeral expenses, this court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.33,000/-.
Altogether, the claimant is entitled for compensation of an amount of Rs.6,69,900/- at 6% interest.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the court has imposed a condition that if the amount is not deposited within 90 days, it would carry 9% interest.
He submits that it is contrary to settled law and the compensation amount shall carry 6% interest.

8. The claimant is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
Sl. Description of Items Compensation Awarded No.
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 5,04,900/-
